strings.name: Alex Krizhevsky
strings.summary: Alex Krizhevsky developed AlexNet with Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton, advancing deep convolutional networks for image recognition. He also helped create the CIFAR datasets and studied multi-GPU training and robotic grasping. He previously worked at Google and served as a technical advisor to Dessa.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. The latest verified participation record is a 2025 museum acknowledgement. Birth date and current position remain unconfirmed; historical roles are not presented as current.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped develop AlexNet, advancing deep convolutional image recognition and influencing subsequent AI research.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: University of Toronto BSc (2007) and MSc (2009).
strings.facts.f2.label: CIFAR collaborators
strings.facts.f2.value: Created CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with Vinod Nair and Geoffrey Hinton.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Visual-recognition breakthrough
strings.highlights.h1.text: AlexNet combined deep convolutional networks with GPU training, helping transform computer vision.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Parallel-training research
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studied multi-GPU training methods for convolutional networks.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Original AlexNet code preserved
strings.timeline.t1.text: CHM and Google release the 2012 source code; the museum thanks him for clarifications.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Dessa announces advisory appointment
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company appoints him technical advisor to support its team’s AI tools.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ends Google employment
strings.timeline.t3.text: His personal page dates the end of his Google employment to this month.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-authors grasping preprint
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Sergey Levine, Peter Pastor and Deirdre Quillen, studies robots learning hand-eye coordination from images.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Releases parallel-training preprint
strings.timeline.t5.text: Proposes training convolutional networks across multiple GPUs.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Google with DNNresearch team
strings.timeline.t6.text: Google acquires the company he co-founded with Hinton and Sutskever; his page confirms this joining month.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-publishes AlexNet paper
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Sutskever and Hinton, reports ImageNet competition results demonstrating large convolutional networks’ potential.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes Toronto master’s degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: His master’s research report examines learning multiple feature layers from tiny images.
